**Proof of security sketch (exact reductions)**:
- Binding: Pedersen vector commitment is computationally binding under discrete-log hardness in G (opening two distinct vectors ⇒ Σ(v-w)_j G_j = O ⇒ nontrivial DLog relation among generators ⇒ solves DLog w.h.p. over random generators). Hence any alteration of any leaf changes some ancestor commitment with overwhelming probability; since each post_root is Ed25519-signed (EUF-CMA under SDH/…—Ed25519 security under standard assumptions) by writer and gate-checked sequentially, altering past entry k forces post_root'_{k} ≠ post_root_k ⇒ signature at k invalid, or attacker forges — breaking Ed25519. Deletion/reorder breaks height-monotonicity check at the gate and the prev_root==parent.post_root equality in audits. Truncation detected against anchored latest root: recomputed root from truncated prefix ≠ anchor unless DLog break.
- Fork/equivocation: identical-height conflicting validly-signed entries constitute transferable proof of double-sign (both sigs are over distinct SIGDOM messages) → automatic slashing/exclusion logic.
- Completeness (no gap): heights strictly consecutive; audit asserts i-th entry has height i.
- External anchoring: publishing (chain_id, height, root, head) to M independent witnesses every Δ entries yields durability: undetected rewrite requires breaking commitments AND controlling all witnesses' logs.

**Definition (Verkle-chained append-only ledger).** A ledger instance is a tuple L = (chain_id, T, E, anchor) where T is a Bandersnatch verkle tree over 32-byte keys/32-byte leaf values, E = (e₁,…,e_h) a strictly increasing sequence of entries with e_k = (k, R_{k−1}, R_k, core_k, σ_k), R₀ = EMPTY_ROOT, R_k = Root(insert(T_{k−1}, k, H(core_k))) for all k∈[1,h], and σ_k a signature on (chain_id,k,R_{k−1},R_k,H'(core_k)) under writer_k ∈ ACL. An anchor A_t = (chain_id, t, R_t, H(e_t), Sig_gate) is any signed checkpoint.
